Марк Аврелий.name: Marcus Aurelius
Марк Аврелий.description: (121–180) Roman Emperor of the Antonine dynasty, one of the greatest Stoic philosophers in history. Born into a noble family and given an excellent education, he was adopted by Emperor Antoninus Pius and groomed as his successor. He became emperor at 40, governing a vast empire while pursuing deep philosophical reflection. He spent much of his reign fighting Germanic tribes and Parthians on the frontiers. His major philosophical work, the 'Meditations,' written in Greek, is a personal diary in which he reflects on Stoic philosophy, duty, virtue, acceptance of fate, and the management of emotions. Marcus practised Stoic principles daily: self-discipline, humility, justice, and service to the common good. Known as the 'philosopher on the throne,' he is a rare example of a ruler who genuinely strove to live according to his principles despite holding enormous power. His reign is regarded as the 'golden age' of the Roman Empire. He died in a military camp at Vindobona (modern Vienna), leaving behind the legacy of a wise ruler and profound thinker.

Илон Маск.name: Elon Musk
Илон Маск.description: Entrepreneur; founder of SpaceX, head of Tesla and X (Twitter).

Павел Дуров.name: Pavel Durov
Павел Дуров.description: Founder of Telegram and VK; entrepreneur and privacy advocate.

Владимир Зеленский.name: Volodymyr Zelenskyy
Владимир Зеленский.description: President of Ukraine; statesman, former actor and producer.

Дональд Трамп.name: Donald Trump
Дональд Трамп.description: 45th and 47th President of the USA, entrepreneur and billionaire.

Александр Македонский.name: Alexander the Great
Александр Македонский.description: (356–323 BC) King of Macedon and one of the greatest military commanders in history. Son of Philip II and Olympias, pupil of Aristotle. He inherited the throne at 20 after his father's assassination. In 13 years of rule he built a vast empire stretching from Greece to India, conquering the Persian Empire, Egypt, and reaching the borders of modern Pakistan. He won decisive battles at Granicus, Issus, and Gaugamela. He founded over 20 cities named Alexandria, the most famous being Alexandria in Egypt. Renowned for his strategic genius, personal bravery in leading cavalry charges, respect for conquered cultures, and his drive to merge East and West. He encouraged intermarriage between Macedonians and Persians and spread Hellenic culture across the known world. He died at 32 in Babylon, most likely from fever, though the exact cause remains debated. After his death the empire fragmented, but his Hellenistic legacy endured for three more centuries. Alexander became a legend in his own lifetime and remains a symbol of military genius, ambition, and the quest for universal dominion.

Альберт Эйнштейн.name: Albert Einstein
Альберт Эйнштейн.description: (1879–1955) German-born theoretical physicist of Jewish origin, one of the founders of modern theoretical physics and Nobel Prize laureate in Physics (1921). Born in Ulm, Germany, in an engineer's family. In childhood he showed no unusual gifts and was even a late talker. He graduated from the Zurich Polytechnic. Working as a patent clerk in Bern, he developed revolutionary physical theories in his spare time. In 1905, his 'miracle year,' he published four papers that transformed physics: the photoelectric effect, Brownian motion, special relativity, and the famous equation E=mc². In 1915 he completed the general theory of relativity, overturning our understanding of space, time, and gravity. He predicted gravitational waves and the bending of light. In 1933, with the Nazi rise to power, he emigrated to the US and joined the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton. He actively opposed Nazism and wrote to Roosevelt about the possibility of an atomic bomb—though he later regretted it. Famous not only as a brilliant scientist but also as a pacifist, humanist, civil rights advocate, and socialist. His iconic image—wild hair, moustache, gentle smile—became a symbol of genius. Einstein transformed our understanding of the universe and remains one of the most influential scientists in history.

Будда.name: Buddha
Будда.description: (c. 563–483 BC) Spiritual teacher, founder of Buddhism, and one of the most influential figures in the history of human thought. Born into a royal family in Lumbini (modern Nepal) with the name Siddhartha. Raised in luxury, but at 29, confronting suffering, illness, old age, and death, he left the palace in search of truth. After six years of asceticism and meditation, at 35 he attained enlightenment (bodhi) beneath the Bodhi tree in Bodh Gaya. After awakening he became known as the Buddha—'the Awakened One.' For 45 years he travelled across India, teaching the Dharma and founding a monastic community (the Sangha). His teaching rests on the Four Noble Truths about suffering and the Eightfold Path to liberation. The Buddha taught that all beings can attain enlightenment through the practice of morality, meditation, and wisdom. He emphasised personal experience over blind faith and the Middle Way between extreme asceticism and sensual indulgence. He died at 80, entering parinirvana. His teaching spread across all of Asia and became one of the world's major religions, with hundreds of millions of followers. The Buddha remains a symbol of wisdom, compassion, and spiritual awakening.

Владимир Ленин.name: Vladimir Lenin
Владимир Ленин.description: (1870–1924) Russian revolutionary, politician, Marxist theorist, and founder and first head of the Soviet state. Born in Simbirsk into the family of a school inspector. His elder brother Alexander was executed for plotting to assassinate the Tsar, which profoundly shaped Vladimir's revolutionary outlook. Expelled from Kazan University for student unrest, he passed bar exams externally and became a lawyer. In 1895 he founded the 'Union of Struggle for the Emancipation of the Working Class,' was arrested, and exiled to Siberia. After exile he emigrated and lived in Switzerland, Germany, France, and England. He developed the theory of imperialism and wrote extensively on Marxism. In 1917, after the February Revolution, he returned to Russia in a sealed railway carriage through Germany. He led the October Revolution and became Chairman of the Council of People's Commissars. During the Civil War he implemented 'war communism,' then introduced the New Economic Policy. He founded the Comintern to spread world revolution. A revolutionary practitioner who combined theoretical work with organisational activity. He died after a series of strokes; his embalmed body lies in a mausoleum on Red Square. Lenin remains one of the most controversial figures of the 20th century: liberator and state-builder to some, tyrant responsible for millions of victims to others.

Джордж Вашингтон.name: George Washington
Джордж Вашингтон.description: (1732–1799) American statesman, first President of the United States (1789–1797), Commander-in-Chief of the Continental Army during the War of Independence, and one of the Founding Fathers. Born in Virginia to a planter family. Home-educated, he worked as a surveyor, then inherited the Mount Vernon plantation. In his youth he served in the Virginia militia and gained military experience in the French and Indian War. In 1759 he married wealthy widow Martha Custis, becoming one of the colony's largest landowners. He was elected to the Virginia House of Burgesses. In 1775 the Continental Congress unanimously elected him commander of the colonial forces. For eight years he waged war against superior British forces, displaying strategic patience, resilience, and the ability to inspire his troops. After victory in 1783 he voluntarily relinquished his command—an unprecedented act for a military leader—and returned to Mount Vernon. In 1787 he presided over the Constitutional Convention. In 1789 he was unanimously elected the first President and re-elected in 1792. He set many precedents: two terms are enough, the address 'Mr President,' the cabinet. In 1796 he refused a third term, establishing a tradition. He died at Mount Vernon. Washington became a symbol of republican virtue, honesty, and voluntary surrender of power; his image on the dollar bill and the capital bearing his name immortalise him as 'Father of his Country.'

Гай Юлий Цезарь.name: Julius Caesar
Гай Юлий Цезарь.description: (100–44 BC) Roman general, politician, writer, and dictator, one of the most influential figures in ancient Roman history. Born into a patrician family, he received an excellent education in Rome and on Rhodes. He began his political career as a tribune of the plebs, then held various offices. He won fame as a military commander during the Gallic Wars (58–50 BC), subduing all of Gaul and making two expeditions to Britain. He wrote the 'Gallic Wars'—a classic of Latin literature. In 49 BC he crossed the Rubicon with the words 'The die is cast,' starting a civil war against Pompey and the Senate. He won at Pharsalus, Thapsus, and Munda, becoming sole ruler of Rome. He reformed the calendar (Julian calendar), expanded citizenship rights, and launched building projects. He was declared perpetual dictator and given the title 'Imperator.' On the Ides of March 44 BC he was assassinated by a group of senators led by Brutus and Cassius, who feared the restoration of monarchy. His death sparked a new civil war and the fall of the Roman Republic. Caesar remains a symbol of military genius, political cunning, and boundless ambition.

Жанна д'Арк.name: Joan of Arc
Жанна д'Арк.description: (c. 1412–1431) National heroine of France, a peasant girl who became a military commander and symbol of French resistance during the Hundred Years' War. Born in Domrémy, Lorraine, to a peasant family. At 13 she began hearing 'voices' of saints (Michael, Catherine, Margaret) urging her to liberate France from the English. At 17, dressed as a man, she reached Dauphin Charles VII at Chinon and persuaded him to give her an army. She led the liberation of Orléans in 1429, which proved a turning point in the war. She participated in the coronation of Charles VII at Reims. Captured by Burgundian allies of the English, she was sold to the English and handed to an ecclesiastical court. Accused of heresy and witchcraft, she was condemned and burned at the stake in Rouen on 30 May 1431 at the age of 19. In 1456 she was rehabilitated, and in 1920 canonised by the Catholic Church. Joan of Arc became a symbol of patriotism, faith, and heroism, inspiring generations of French people and remaining one of the most famous women in history.

Иисус.name: Jesus
Иисус.description: (c. 4 BC – 30 AD) Central figure of Christianity, preacher, teacher, and messiah whose teachings form the foundation of one of the world's largest religions. Born in Bethlehem, raised in Nazareth, Galilee, in the family of a carpenter named Joseph and Mary. Little is known of his childhood apart from an episode in the temple at age 12. He began his public ministry around age 30, preaching in Galilee and Judea. His teaching included parables about the Kingdom of God, commandments of love for God and neighbour, and calls to repentance and new life. He performed miracles: healings, resurrections, walking on water, turning water into wine. He gathered a group of 12 apostles. He entered Jerusalem as messiah and cleansed the temple of merchants. He was betrayed by Judas Iscariot, arrested, tried, and sentenced to crucifixion by the Roman prefect Pontius Pilate. Crucified at Golgotha, he died and, according to Christian belief, rose on the third day. His life, death, and resurrection became the foundation of Christian faith, changing the course of world history. Jesus remains one of the most influential figures in human history.

Иосиф Сталин.name: Joseph Stalin
Иосиф Сталин.description: (1878–1953) Soviet statesman, politician, and military figure, Generalissimo and leader of the USSR from the mid-1920s until 1953. Born in Gori, Georgia, to a cobbler's family. He studied at the Tiflis Theological Seminary but was expelled for revolutionary activity. He joined the Bolsheviks, participated in the 1905 Revolution, and was repeatedly arrested and exiled. After the October Revolution he held various posts and in 1922 became General Secretary of the Central Committee. After Lenin's death in 1924 he gradually consolidated power, eliminating rivals (Trotsky, Zinoviev, Kamenev). He conducted industrialisation, collectivisation of agriculture, and the Great Terror of the 1930s. During the Great Patriotic War he headed the State Defence Committee and coordinated military operations. After the war he contributed to the creation of the socialist bloc and the start of the Cold War. He died in 1953. His period in power was characterised by mass repression and a cult of personality, but also by industrial development and victory in the war. Stalin remains one of the most controversial figures of the 20th century.

Клеопатра.name: Cleopatra
Клеопатра.description: (69–30 BC) Last queen of the Hellenistic Egypt of the Ptolemaic dynasty, one of the most famous women in history. Born in Alexandria, she received an excellent education and spoke many languages. In 51 BC she became co-ruler with her brother Ptolemy XIII, but was driven out. She returned with the help of Julius Caesar, becoming his lover and bearing his son Caesarion. After Caesar's death she allied with Mark Antony, becoming his wife and bearing three children. Together with Antony she opposed Octavian (the future emperor Augustus) in the struggle for power over Rome. After defeat at the Battle of Actium in 31 BC and Antony's suicide, Cleopatra killed herself, according to legend by the bite of a venomous asp. Her death marked the end of Hellenistic Egypt and the beginning of Roman rule. Cleopatra is famous for her beauty, intelligence, erudition, diplomatic skill, and romantic liaisons with the two greatest Romans of her age. She became a symbol of female power, seduction, and tragic fate.

Христофор Колумб.name: Christopher Columbus
Христофор Колумб.description: (1451–1506) Italian navigator, admiral, viceroy, and governor of the Indies who opened the Americas to Europeans. Born in Genoa, Italy, to a weaver's family. From youth he was a sailor and navigated the Mediterranean. He developed a plan to reach India by sailing westward across the Atlantic, based on the idea of the Earth's spherical shape. After years of seeking patronage, he won the support of Spanish monarchs Ferdinand and Isabella. On 3 August 1492 he set sail from Palos with three ships (Santa María, Pinta, Niña) and 90 sailors. On 12 October 1492 he reached the island of San Salvador (Bahamas), discovering the New World—though he believed he had reached Asia. He made three more voyages (1493, 1498, 1502), discovering the Caribbean islands, Central America, and South America, and founded the first European colonies in the Americas. He died in Valladolid, never knowing he had discovered a new continent. His discoveries launched the Age of Exploration, the colonisation of the Americas, and the global exchange between the Old and New Worlds. Columbus remains a symbol of courage, adventure, and the era of discovery.

Леонардо да Винчи.name: Leonardo da Vinci
Леонардо да Винчи.description: (1452–1519) Italian painter, scientist, engineer, inventor, anatomist, and Renaissance polymath, one of the greatest geniuses in human history. Born in Vinci, near Florence, the illegitimate son of a notary. He studied under Verrocchio in Florence, developing his artistic and technical skills. He worked in Milan, Florence, Rome, and France. He created famous paintings: the 'Mona Lisa' (La Gioconda), 'The Last Supper,' 'Madonna of the Rocks.' He carried out extensive scientific research: anatomy (dissecting corpses), physics, mechanics, hydraulics, botany, and geology. He produced thousands of drawings and mirror-script notes containing inventions: flying machines, submarines, tanks, and mechanisms. He studied the flight of birds and designed bridges, canals, and military machines. His approach united art and science, observation and experiment. He served as court engineer and painter for the Duke of Milan, then for the French king Francis I. He died in France, leaving an enormous legacy of unfinished projects and ideas that were centuries ahead of their time. Leonardo remains the ultimate symbol of universal genius and boundless curiosity.

Мартин Лютер Кинг-младший.name: Martin Luther King Jr.
Мартин Лютер Кинг-младший.description: (1929–1968) American Baptist pastor, activist, and leader of the African-American civil rights movement, Nobel Peace Prize laureate (1964). Born in Atlanta, Georgia, to a pastor's family. He earned a doctorate in theology from Boston University. In 1955 he led the Montgomery bus boycott after Rosa Parks's arrest. He became the leader of the civil rights movement and founded the Southern Christian Leadership Conference. He organised mass nonviolent protests: marches, sit-ins, and voting-rights campaigns. He delivered the famous 'I Have a Dream' speech in 1963 at the March on Washington. He played a key role in passing the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and the Voting Rights Act of 1965. He spoke out against the Vietnam War and poverty. On 4 April 1968 he was assassinated in Memphis, Tennessee. His philosophy of nonviolence (satyagraha), inspired by Gandhi, and his oratory made him a symbol of the struggle for equality and justice. King remains one of the most revered figures in American history.

Наполеон Бонапарт.name: Napoleon Bonaparte
Наполеон Бонапарт.description: (1769–1821) French military commander and statesman, Emperor of the French (1804–1814, 1815), one of the greatest military leaders in history. Born in Corsica to a minor noble family. He studied at military schools in France and became an artillery officer. He first distinguished himself during the siege of Toulon in 1793 and rose rapidly through the ranks. In 1796–1797 he conducted the brilliant Italian Campaign, routing the Austrians. In 1798–1799 he led the Egyptian Expedition. In 1799 he staged a coup (18 Brumaire), becoming First Consul, and in 1804 proclaimed himself Emperor. He enacted administrative, legal (the Napoleonic Code), educational, and financial reforms. He waged numerous wars, creating a vast empire stretching from Spain to Russia. He won at Austerlitz, Jena, and Wagram, but suffered defeat in Russia (1812) and at Waterloo (1815). He abdicated twice and was exiled to Saint Helena, where he died. Napoleon changed the political map of Europe, spread the ideas of the French Revolution, and created a modern system of government. He remains a symbol of military genius, ambition, and the romantic era.

Стив Джобс.name: Steve Jobs
Стив Джобс.description: (1955–2011) American entrepreneur and visionary, co-founder of Apple Inc. and pioneer of the personal computer era. Born in San Francisco and adopted by Paul and Clara Jobs, he grew up in the Silicon Valley area. He dropped out of Reed College but continued to audit classes including calligraphy, which later influenced Apple's typography. In 1976, together with Steve Wozniak, he co-founded Apple Computer and helped popularise the personal computer with the Apple II and later the Macintosh. Forced out of Apple in 1985, he founded NeXT and acquired Pixar, which produced groundbreaking animated films under his leadership. Returning to Apple in 1997, he led a dramatic turnaround, overseeing the creation of the iMac, iPod, iTunes, iPhone, and iPad. His philosophy united technology and liberal arts, insisting on elegant design and intuitive interfaces that changed how billions of people interact with technology. He was known for his passionate presentations and uncompromising pursuit of perfection. He died from pancreatic cancer, leaving behind a transformative legacy that continues to shape the technology industry.

Уинстон Черчилль.name: Winston Churchill
Уинстон Черчилль.description: (1874–1965) British statesman, Prime Minister of the United Kingdom (1940–1945, 1951–1955), war correspondent, writer, and Nobel Prize laureate in Literature. Born into an aristocratic family, son of Lord Randolph Churchill. He was educated at Harrow and Sandhurst and served in wars in India, Sudan, and South Africa. He was a war correspondent and wrote many books. He entered politics in 1900 and held various ministerial posts. In 1940, at a critical moment of the Second World War, he became Prime Minister and led a coalition government. His speeches inspired the nation: 'Blood, toil, tears and sweat'; 'We shall fight on the beaches.' He worked with Roosevelt and Stalin in the 'Big Three.' After the war he warned of the 'Iron Curtain' and the start of the Cold War. He lost the 1945 election but returned to power in 1951. He was famous for his wit, love of cigars and brandy, stubbornness, and unshakeable faith in Britain. He died in 1965. Churchill remains a symbol of leadership in times of crisis and one of the greatest orators of the 20th century.

Чингисхан.name: Genghis Khan
Чингисхан.description: (c. 1162–1227) Founder and first Great Khan of the Mongol Empire, one of the greatest conquerors in history. Born into the family of a Mongol clan chief, he suffered his father's murder, captivity, and poverty in childhood. He united the scattered Mongol tribes, creating a powerful military organisation. In 1206 he was proclaimed Genghis Khan—'Universal Ruler.' He established the Yasa code, reorganised the army on a decimal system, and introduced strict discipline. He began a series of conquests, subduing northern China, Central Asia, Persia, and part of Eastern Europe. His empire became the largest contiguous land empire in history. He is known for ferocity in war, but also for religious tolerance, promotion of trade, and the creation of an efficient administrative system. He died during a campaign against the Tanguts. His empire was divided among his sons, but Mongol influence spread across vast territories. Genghis Khan remains a symbol of military genius, unification, and empire-building.

Чарльз Дарвин.name: Charles Darwin
Чарльз Дарвин.description: (1809–1882) English naturalist, geologist, and biologist, originator of the theory of evolution by natural selection. Born in Shrewsbury to a doctor's family. He studied medicine in Edinburgh and theology in Cambridge, but became captivated by natural history. In 1831–1836 he made a round-the-world voyage on HMS Beagle, collecting a vast sample collection and making observations that underpinned his theory. He studied the geology of the Galápagos Islands, the fauna and flora of South America, and fossils. In 1859 he published 'On the Origin of Species,' setting out the theory of natural selection as the mechanism of evolution. The theory explained the diversity of life through common descent and adaptation to environmental conditions. It provoked fierce debate, contradicting religious beliefs about creation. He later published 'The Descent of Man' (1871), applying the theory to humans. Darwin was a modest, methodical scientist who carefully gathered evidence. His theory became the foundation of modern biology and changed our understanding of humanity's place in nature. He died in Downe, Kent. Darwin remains one of the most influential scientists in history.

Винсент Ван Гог.name: Vincent van Gogh
Винсент Ван Гог.description: (1853–1890) Dutch Post-Impressionist painter, one of the most famous and influential artists in history. Born in Groot-Zundert, Netherlands, to a pastor's family. He worked as an art dealer, teacher, and preacher among poor miners before deciding to become a painter in 1880. He studied in Brussels, Antwerp, and Paris. He lived in poverty, supported by his brother Theo. He created over 2,000 works: paintings, drawings, and sketches. He developed a unique style with vivid colours, expressive brushstrokes, and emotional intensity. Famous works include 'The Starry Night,' 'Sunflowers,' 'Bedroom in Arles,' and 'The Night Café.' In 1888 he moved to Arles, where he produced his finest works. He suffered from mental illness and in 1888 cut off part of his own ear. He was treated in psychiatric clinics. On 27 July 1890 he shot himself in the chest and died two days later. During his lifetime he sold only one painting, but after his death his work gained worldwide recognition. Van Gogh became a symbol of the suffering genius whose art reflects the depth of human emotion and the beauty of the world.

Уильям Шекспир.name: William Shakespeare
Уильям Шекспир.description: (1564–1616) English poet, playwright, and actor, the greatest writer in the English language and one of the world's foremost dramatists. Born in Stratford-upon-Avon to a glove-maker's family. He was educated at the local grammar school. At 18 he married Anne Hathaway and had three children. Around 1590 he moved to London and began a career as an actor and playwright. He became a shareholder in the theatrical company 'Lord Chamberlain's Men,' later renamed 'King's Men.' He wrote 37 plays: tragedies ('Hamlet,' 'King Lear,' 'Macbeth,' 'Othello'), comedies ('A Midsummer Night's Dream,' 'Twelfth Night,' 'The Merchant of Venice'), and history plays. He composed 154 sonnets and several narrative poems. His works explore human nature, passion, power, love, jealousy, and ambition. He introduced thousands of new words and phrases into English. He died in Stratford and was buried in the local church. Debate about his authorship continues, but his influence on literature, theatre, and culture is undisputed. Shakespeare remains a symbol of genius and the supreme master of language.

Вольфганг Амадей Моцарт.name: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart
Вольфганг Амадей Моцарт.description: (1756–1791) Austrian composer and musician, one of the greatest composers in musical history, a child prodigy and genius of the Classical era. Born in Salzburg to composer and violinist Leopold Mozart. At 3 he began playing the harpsichord; at 5 he started composing. At 6, together with his sister Nannerl, he embarked on concert tours of Europe, astonishing royal courts with his talent. He met emperors, kings, and the Pope. He wrote more than 600 works: operas ('Don Giovanni,' 'The Magic Flute,' 'The Marriage of Figaro'), symphonies, concertos, chamber music, masses, and requiems. He served at the court of the Archbishop of Salzburg, then worked as a freelance musician in Vienna. He married Constanze Weber and had six children (two survived). Despite his genius he lived in financial difficulty. He died at 35 in Vienna, probably from rheumatic fever, leaving his Requiem unfinished. Mozart combined virtuosity, melodic gift, emotional depth, and structural perfection. His music remains among the most performed and beloved in the world.

Зигмунд Фрейд.name: Sigmund Freud
Зигмунд Фрейд.description: (1856–1939) Austrian neurologist, founder of psychoanalysis, and one of the most influential figures in the history of psychology and psychiatry. Born in Freiberg, Moravia (now Czech Republic), to a Jewish family. At 3 he moved to Vienna, where he spent most of his life. He studied medicine at the University of Vienna, specialising in neurology. He worked with Jean Charcot in Paris, studying hysteria and hypnosis. He developed the method of free association and dream analysis. In 1899 he published 'The Interpretation of Dreams,' the founding work of psychoanalysis. He created the model of the psyche: the Id (unconscious), the Ego (consciousness), and the Superego (moral conscience). He introduced the concepts of repression, sublimation, the Oedipus complex, libido, and thanatos. He developed the theory of infantile sexuality, the significance of the unconscious, and the role of dreams and slips of the tongue. He founded the International Psychoanalytic Association. His ideas influenced literature, art, anthropology, and sociology. In 1938, after Austria's annexation, he emigrated to London. He died of jaw cancer. Freud remains a controversial but fundamental figure in our understanding of the human psyche.

Исаак Ньютон.name: Isaac Newton
Исаак Ньютон.description: (1643–1727) English mathematician, physicist, astronomer, alchemist, and philosopher, one of the greatest scientists in history. Born in Woolsthorpe, Lincolnshire, to a farming family. His father died before his birth; his mother left him with his grandmother. He studied at Cambridge University, where he became Professor of Mathematics. In 1687 he published 'Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica'—one of the greatest scientific works ever written. He formulated three laws of motion and the law of universal gravitation, explaining planetary motion and falling apples. He developed differential and integral calculus (simultaneously with Leibniz). He studied optics, decomposed white light into a spectrum, and built the first reflecting telescope. He discovered the binomial theorem and methods of approximate calculation. He was Director of the Royal Mint and reformed England's monetary system. He was President of the Royal Society. He also pursued alchemy and theology, writing more about religion than science. He was reclusive and solitary, often quarrelling with Hooke and Leibniz. He died in London and was buried in Westminster Abbey. Newton laid the foundations of classical mechanics and mathematics, transforming our understanding of the universe.

Карл Маркс.name: Karl Marx
Карл Маркс.description: (1818–1883) German philosopher, economist, sociologist, political journalist, and revolutionary theorist, founding father of Marxism. Born in Trier, Prussia, to a Jewish family that had converted to Lutheranism. He studied law, philosophy, and history in Bonn and Berlin, earning a doctorate in philosophy from Jena. He worked as a journalist, editing the 'Rheinische Zeitung.' In 1843 he married Jenny von Westphalen, moved to Paris, then Brussels, and finally London. In 1848, together with Engels, he wrote 'The Communist Manifesto'—the programme document of the communist movement. His main work is 'Capital' (Vol. 1, 1867), an analysis of the capitalist mode of production. He developed historical materialism, the theory of class struggle, surplus value, and labour alienation. He founded the First International (1864). He lived in poverty in London, supported by Engels. His ideas influenced the labour movement, socialist and communist parties, and the revolutions of the 20th century. He died in London and is buried at Highgate Cemetery. Marx remains one of the most influential and controversial figures in the history of thought.

Лев Толстой.name: Leo Tolstoy
Лев Толстой.description: (1828–1910) Russian writer, thinker, moral philosopher, and public figure, one of the greatest writers in world literary history. Born at Yasnaya Polyana, Tula Province, into an aristocratic family. He was orphaned early and raised by relatives. He studied at Kazan University but did not graduate. He participated in the Crimean War and served in the Caucasus. In 1862 he married Sophia Bers and had 13 children. He wrote the greatest novels: 'War and Peace' (1869)—an epic about Russia in the Napoleonic era—and 'Anna Karenina' (1877)—a novel about love and society. He produced many novellas, stories, plays, and pedagogical and philosophical writings. In the 1880s he experienced a spiritual crisis and developed a doctrine of non-resistance to evil through violence, criticising the Church and the state. He founded a school for peasant children, preached simple living, vegetarianism, and renunciation of property. He was excommunicated by the Church in 1901. His ideas influenced Gandhi and the nonviolence movement. At 82 he secretly left Yasnaya Polyana and died at Astapovo station. Tolstoy remains a symbol of moral searching and humanism.

Людвиг ван Бетховен.name: Ludwig van Beethoven
Людвиг ван Бетховен.description: (1770–1827) German composer and pianist, one of the greatest composers in musical history, a pivotal figure bridging Classicism and Romanticism. Born in Bonn to the family of a court musician. He studied under his father, then under Christian Gottlob Neefe. At 22 he moved to Vienna, where he studied under Haydn, Salieri, and Albrechtsberger. He became famous as a virtuosic pianist and improviser. At 26 he began to lose his hearing and was completely deaf by 44, yet continued to compose. He wrote 9 symphonies (including the famous Ninth with the 'Ode to Joy'), 5 piano concertos, 32 piano sonatas, 16 string quartets, the opera 'Fidelio,' and the 'Missa Solemnis.' His music is characterised by emotional intensity, drama, heroic pathos, and the overcoming of suffering. He was solitary and never married, enduring deafness and illness. He died in Vienna; 20,000 people attended his funeral. Beethoven pushed the boundaries of musical form and expressivity and became a symbol of the triumph of the human spirit over adversity.

Михаил Булгаков.name: Mikhail Bulgakov
Михаил Булгаков.description: (1891–1940) Russian and Soviet writer, playwright, theatrical director, and actor, one of the greatest Russian writers of the 20th century. Born in Kyiv to the family of a professor of the Kyiv Theological Academy. He graduated from the Medical Faculty of Kyiv University and worked as a doctor during World War I and the Civil War. In 1921 he moved to Moscow and abandoned medicine for literature. He wrote satirical novellas: 'Diaboliad,' 'The Fatal Eggs,' 'The Heart of a Dog.' He created plays for the Moscow Art Theatre: 'The Days of the Turbins,' 'Zoyka's Apartment,' 'Flight.' His masterpiece is the novel 'The Master and Margarita' (1928–1940), combining satire, fantasy, philosophy, and biblical motifs. The novel was published only in 1966–1967, 26 years after the author's death. He also wrote 'The White Guard,' 'A Theatrical Novel,' and a biography of Molière. His works were subjected to criticism and bans in the USSR. He died of hereditary kidney disease in Moscow. Bulgakov remains a master of satire, mysticism, and deep psychological insight, a symbol of creative freedom under totalitarianism.

Михаил Ломоносов.name: Mikhail Lomonosov
Михаил Ломоносов.description: (1711–1765) Russia's first world-class natural scientist, an encyclopaedist, physicist, chemist, astronomer, geologist, metallurgist, poet, philologist, painter, and historian. Born in the village of Mishaninsk (now Lomonosovo), Arkhangelsk Province, to a peasant fisherman's family. At 19 he walked to Moscow with a merchant convoy, posing as a nobleman's son to gain entry to the Slavo-Greco-Latin Academy. He graduated from there, then studied at the St Petersburg Academy and in Germany. Returning to Russia, he became Professor of Chemistry at the Academy of Sciences. He set up Russia's first chemical laboratory, founded glass manufacturing, developed coloured glass and mosaic-making technology. He formulated the law of conservation of mass, developed a corpuscular theory, and studied atmospheric electricity. He founded Moscow University (1755). He wrote odes, tragedies, and satires, and created the theory of 'three styles' in Russian literature. He reformed the Russian language and created scientific terminology. He studied Russian history and wrote 'Ancient Russian History.' He died in St Petersburg. Lomonosov became the symbol of the Russian Enlightenment and universal genius.

Пабло Пикассо.name: Pablo Picasso
Пабло Пикассо.description: (1881–1973) Spanish-French painter, sculptor, printmaker, ceramicist, and designer, one of the greatest and most influential artists of the 20th century. Born in Málaga, Spain, to a painter and art teacher. He displayed exceptional talent from childhood. He studied in Barcelona and Madrid. In 1900 he first visited Paris and in 1904 moved there permanently. His career passed through several periods: the Blue Period (1901–1904)—melancholic paintings in blue tones; the Rose Period (1904–1906)—lighter works with harlequins; and the African Period (1907–1909)—influenced by African art. In 1907 he created 'Les Demoiselles d'Avignon,' the painting that launched Cubism, a revolutionary approach in which objects are depicted from multiple viewpoints simultaneously. Together with Braque he developed Analytic and Synthetic Cubism. He created more than 50,000 works: paintings, sculptures, ceramics, and prints. He painted the famous 'Guernica' (1937), an anti-war masterpiece. He was a member of the Communist Party. He died in Mougins, France. Picasso changed our understanding of art by shattering traditional forms and creating new ways of seeing the world.

Сальвадор Дали.name: Salvador Dalí
Сальвадор Дали.description: (1904–1989) Spanish painter, one of the most famous representatives of Surrealism, master of provocation and shock. Born in Figueres, Catalonia, to a notary's family. He studied at the Madrid Academy of Fine Arts and was expelled for insubordination. In 1929 he joined the Surrealists in Paris and met his muse and wife Gala (Elena Diakonova). He developed the 'paranoiac-critical method'—a way of creating images through delirious associations. He produced famous paintings: 'The Persistence of Memory' (melting clocks), 'Dream Caused by the Flight of a Bee,' 'The Face of War,' and 'Christ of Saint John of the Cross.' He collaborated in cinema with Buñuel ('Un Chien Andalou') and with Walt Disney. He created sculptures, jewellery, stage designs, and book illustrations. He was famous for his eccentric behaviour, his moustache, and provocative pronouncements. In the 1940s he broke with the Surrealists and turned to classical themes and religious subjects. He lived in the US, then returned to Spain. He died in Figueres, where he had created his Theatre-Museum. Dalí remains a symbol of Surrealism and a master of dream-like imagery.

Сократ.name: Socrates
Сократ.description: (470–399 BC) Ancient Greek philosopher from Athens, one of the founders of Western philosophy and teacher of Plato. Born in Athens, son of sculptor Sophroniscus and midwife Phaenarete. He took part in the Peloponnesian War and showed courage. He left no written works; his teaching is known through the dialogues of Plato and Xenophon. He developed the method of dialogue and questioning (maieutics—the 'midwife's art'), helping interlocutors find truth through questions. Famous for the sayings 'I know that I know nothing' and 'Know thyself.' He explored questions of virtue, justice, the good, and knowledge. He criticised the Sophists for false wisdom, exposing contradictions in their reasoning. He was accused of corrupting the youth and impiety, condemned to death, and drank hemlock. His death became a symbol of fidelity to principles and readiness to die for truth. Socrates influenced Plato, Aristotle, and all of Western philosophy. He remains a symbol of philosophical inquiry, irony, and moral excellence.

Фёдор Достоевский.name: Fyodor Dostoevsky
Фёдор Достоевский.description: (1821–1881) Russian writer, thinker, philosopher, and journalist, one of the greatest novelists in world literary history. Born in Moscow to a military doctor's family. He studied at the Engineering Academy in St Petersburg but left the service for literature. He debuted with the novel 'Poor Folk' (1846). In 1849 he was arrested for membership in the Petrashevsky Circle, sentenced to death, but reprieved at the last moment and sent to hard labour in Siberia (1850–1854), then to the army. He returned to St Petersburg in 1859. He wrote his greatest novels: 'Crime and Punishment' (1866), 'The Idiot' (1868), 'Demons' (1872), 'The Adolescent' (1875), 'The Brothers Karamazov' (1880). He explored the depths of the human soul, the problems of freedom, faith, suffering, good, and evil. He suffered from epilepsy, which influenced his writing. He was a passionate gambler and often in debt. He travelled in Europe and criticised Western civilisation. He died in St Petersburg. Dostoevsky remains the master of psychological analysis, explorer of the human 'underground,' and one of the greatest philosopher-novelists.

Конфуций.name: Confucius
Конфуций.description: (551–479 BC) Chinese philosopher, teacher, and statesman, founder of Confucianism, one of China's principal philosophical systems. Born in Qufu, State of Lu (now Shandong Province), to an impoverished aristocratic family. Orphaned early, he was raised by his mother. He received an education, worked as an official, and founded a private school open to all regardless of background. He wandered through China offering his services to rulers but never obtained a high post. He returned to Lu, where he taught and edited classical texts. His teaching is presented in the 'Analects' ('Lunyu')—a collection of sayings compiled by disciples. Confucian philosophy is based on ethics, ritual (li), benevolence (ren), filial piety (xiao), and righteousness (yi). His concept of the 'gentleman' (junzi)—the ideal of a moral person—emphasised education, self-cultivation, and correct relationships in family and society. He died in Qufu. Confucianism became the foundation of Chinese statehood and culture for two millennia. Confucius remains a symbol of wisdom and moral excellence.

Махатма Ганди.name: Mahatma Gandhi
Махатма Ганди.description: (1869–1948) Indian political and spiritual leader, originator of the philosophy of nonviolence (satyagraha), and father of the Indian nation. Born in Porbandar, Gujarat, to a minister's family. At 19 he went to London to study law. He worked as a lawyer in South Africa (1893–1914), encountered racial discrimination, and began fighting for the rights of Indians. He developed the method of nonviolent resistance (satyagraha). He returned to India in 1915 and became the leader of the independence movement. He organised mass campaigns: boycott of British goods, the Salt March (1930), and the 'Quit India' movement (1942). He conducted hunger strikes and served time in jail. He preached simplicity, self-restraint, hand-spinning (charkha), and Hindu-Muslim unity. In 1947 India gained independence but was partitioned into India and Pakistan. On 30 January 1948 he was assassinated by a Hindu extremist in Delhi. Gandhi inspired civil rights movements worldwide, including Martin Luther King. He remains a symbol of nonviolence, simplicity, and spiritual power.

Николай Коперник.name: Nicolaus Copernicus
Николай Коперник.description: (1473–1543) Polish astronomer, mathematician, canon, physician, and economist, creator of the heliocentric model of the universe, who revolutionised astronomy. Born in Toruń, Kingdom of Poland, to a merchant's family. Orphaned early, he was raised by his uncle the bishop. He studied at Kraków University, then in Italy (Bologna, Padua, Ferrara), studying law, medicine, and astronomy. He earned a doctorate in canon law. Returning to Poland, he became a canon of the Warmia Chapter, handling administrative duties and treating the sick. In his spare time he pursued astronomy, making observations and calculations. He developed a heliocentric model of the universe, with the Sun at the centre and the Earth and other planets revolving around it—contradicting Ptolemy's geocentric system, accepted for over 1,400 years. He published 'De revolutionibus orbium coelestium' in 1543, the year of his death, from fear of persecution. The book was dedicated to Pope Paul III. Copernicus also worked in economics and formulated a law on money. His discovery launched the Scientific Revolution and changed our understanding of humanity's place in the universe. He remains a symbol of scientific courage and the pursuit of truth.

Мария Склодовская-Кюри.name: Marie Curie
Мария Склодовская-Кюри.description: (1867–1934) Polish-French experimental scientist, physicist, and chemist, the first woman to win a Nobel Prize and the only scientist to be awarded the Nobel Prize in two different scientific disciplines. Born in Warsaw, Kingdom of Poland, to a teacher's family. She could not study at Warsaw University (women were forbidden), so she worked as a governess to help her sister study in Paris. In 1891 she enrolled at the Sorbonne, where she studied physics and mathematics. In 1895 she married Pierre Curie, with whom she worked for the rest of her life. Together they discovered new elements: polonium (named after Poland) and radium. In 1903 she, Pierre Curie, and Henri Becquerel shared the Nobel Prize in Physics for research into radioactivity. After her husband's death in 1906 she continued her work and became the first female professor at the Sorbonne. In 1911 she received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for the discovery of radium and polonium and for isolating pure radium. During the First World War she organised mobile X-ray units. She died of aplastic anaemia caused by prolonged exposure to radiation. Curie became a symbol of scientific perseverance, breaking down gender barriers, and self-sacrifice in the service of science.

Никола Тесла.name: Nikola Tesla
Никола Тесла.description: (1856–1943) Serbian-American inventor, electrical and mechanical engineer, and physicist, one of the greatest inventors in history. Born in Smiljan, Austrian Empire (now Croatia), to an Orthodox priest's family. He studied engineering in Graz and Prague. He worked in Budapest and Paris, then emigrated to the US in 1884. He worked for Thomas Edison but left over disagreements. He founded his own laboratory. He developed the alternating current (AC) system, which defeated Edison's direct current (DC) in the 'War of Currents.' He invented the induction motor, transformer, and multiphase power transmission systems. He created the Tesla coil—a device for generating high voltage. He experimented with wireless power transmission, radio, X-rays, and remote control. He built the Wardenclyffe Tower on Long Island for wireless energy transmission. He held more than 300 patents. He was a visionary who predicted many future technologies. He lived eccentrically, suffered from obsessive-compulsive disorder, and adored pigeons. He died in poverty in New York. Tesla remains a symbol of genius, inventiveness, and visionary thinking.

Архимед.name: Archimedes
Архимед.description: (c. 287–212 BC) Ancient Greek mathematician, physicist, engineer, inventor, and astronomer from Syracuse, one of the greatest scientists of antiquity. Born in Syracuse, Sicily, to an astronomer's family. He studied in Alexandria, the centre of Hellenistic science. Returning to Syracuse, he served at the court of King Hiero II. He made fundamental contributions to mathematics: calculated π with high accuracy, developed the method of exhaustion for computing areas and volumes, and laid the foundations of integral calculus. He formulated Archimedes' principle of buoyancy (the legendary bathtub and 'Eureka!'). He invented the Archimedes screw for raising water, and military machines (catapults, 'Archimedes' Claw,' burning mirrors). During the Roman siege of Syracuse (214–212 BC) he organised the defence with powerful machines. After the city fell he was killed by a Roman soldier despite orders to spare his life. Archimedes united theoretical mathematics with practical engineering, laying the foundations of many sciences. He remains a symbol of genius that joins theory and practice.

Елизавета II.name: Elizabeth II
Елизавета II.description: (1926–2022) Queen of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland and other Commonwealth Realms from 1952 to 2022, the longest-reigning British monarch in history (70 years). Born in London as Princess Elizabeth Alexandra Mary, elder daughter of the Duke of York (future King George VI). She was not expected to become queen, but after her uncle Edward VIII's abdication in 1936 her father became king. During the Second World War she served in the Women's Auxiliary Territorial Service. In 1947 she married Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh, and had four children. She became queen at 25 after her father's death. During her reign she knew 15 prime ministers, from Churchill to Truss. She witnessed the dissolution of the British Empire, the Cold War, and Britain's entry into and exit from the EU. She made hundreds of state visits and became a symbol of stability and continuity. She celebrated Silver, Golden, Diamond, and Platinum Jubilees. She died at Balmoral, Scotland. Elizabeth II remains a symbol of service, dignity, and the monarchy's adaptation to modernity.

Маргарет Тэтчер.name: Margaret Thatcher
Маргарет Тэтчер.description: (1925–2013) British politician, the first female Prime Minister of the United Kingdom (1979–1990), leader of the Conservative Party, and the 'Iron Lady.' Born in Grantham, Lincolnshire, to a grocer and Methodist lay preacher. She graduated from Oxford University, studying chemistry then law. She worked as a research chemist, then as a barrister. Elected to Parliament in 1959. She served as Secretary of State for Education (1970–1974) and Leader of the Opposition (1975–1979). In 1979 she became Prime Minister—the first woman to hold that office in Europe. She carried out radical economic reforms (Thatcherism): privatisation of state enterprises, tax cuts, restriction of trade unions, and financial deregulation. She won the Falklands War (1982). She was re-elected in 1983 and 1987. She was Ronald Reagan's ally in the Cold War and contributed to its end. She resigned in 1990 due to intra-party disagreements. She was made a Baroness. She died in London. Thatcher transformed Britain's economy and politics, becoming a symbol of decisive leadership and the free market. She remains one of the most influential and controversial figures in British politics.

Франклин Делано Рузвельт.name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
Франклин Делано Рузвельт.description: (1882–1945) 32nd President of the United States (1933–1945), the only president elected to four terms, and the leader of the nation during the Great Depression and the Second World War. Born in Hyde Park, New York, into a wealthy aristocratic family. He was a distant cousin of President Theodore Roosevelt. He graduated from Harvard and Columbia Law School. In 1910 he was elected to the New York state senate; in 1913–1920 he was Assistant Secretary of the Navy. In 1921 he contracted polio and lost the ability to walk, but concealed his disability from the public. In 1928 he was elected Governor of New York. In 1932 he was elected President at the height of the Great Depression. He enacted the 'New Deal'—a programme of economic reform: job creation, social insurance, bank regulation, and aid to farmers. In 1941, after the attack on Pearl Harbor, he led the US into the Second World War. He worked with Churchill and Stalin in the 'Big Three,' planning the post-war world. He articulated the 'Four Freedoms': freedom of speech and worship, freedom from fear and want. He died in April 1945, not living to see the end of the war. Roosevelt restored Americans' faith in democracy and government and remains one of the greatest presidents of the United States.

Генри Форд.name: Henry Ford
Генри Форд.description: (1863–1947) American industrialist, inventor, and businessman, founder of the Ford Motor Company, creator of the assembly line that revolutionised the automobile industry. Born on a farm in Greenfield Township, Michigan, to Irish immigrant parents. From childhood he was fascinated by machinery. At 16 he left home for Detroit to work as a machinist. In 1891 he became an engineer at Edison Illuminating Company. In his spare time he built automobiles. In 1896 he created his first car, the quadricycle. In 1903 he founded the Ford Motor Company. In 1908 he introduced the Model T—a simple, reliable, and affordable automobile. In 1913 he introduced the assembly line, revolutionising industry. He reduced assembly time from 12 hours to 1.5 hours. In 1914 he introduced the 8-hour working day and a minimum wage of five dollars a day—twice the average. He produced millions of automobiles, making them accessible to the middle class. He was an anti-Semite and opponent of trade unions but also a philanthropist. He died in Dearborn, Michigan. Ford transformed not only the automobile industry but the entire way of life, creating an era of mass production and mobility.

Рафаэль Санти.name: Raphael
Рафаэль Санти.description: (1483–1520) Italian painter and architect of the High Renaissance, one of the greatest masters in the history of art. Born in Urbino to painter Giovanni Santi. Orphaned early, he studied under Perugino. He worked in Florence, where he absorbed the work of Leonardo and Michelangelo, then in Rome at the invitation of Pope Julius II. He decorated the Stanze of the Vatican ('The School of Athens,' 'Disputation,' 'Parnassus'), created the 'Sistine Madonna' and many Madonnas that became the standard of harmony and noble beauty. He synthesised the achievements of his predecessors into a clear and exalted style. He became chief architect of St Peter's Basilica after Bramante's death. He maintained a large workshop with dozens of pupils. He died in Rome on his 37th birthday, leaving the 'Transfiguration' unfinished. Raphael embodies the ideal of the High Renaissance—harmony, nobility, and perfection of form.

Томас Эдисон.name: Thomas Edison
Томас Эдисон.description: (1847–1931) American inventor and entrepreneur, one of the greatest innovators in history. Born in Milan, Ohio, to a labourer's family. Partially deaf from childhood, this did not hinder his career. He worked as a telegraph operator and was self-educated. In 1868 he received his first patent. In 1876 he founded a laboratory in Menlo Park, New Jersey—the world's first industrial research laboratory. He invented the phonograph (1877), improved the incandescent lamp (1879), and created an electric lighting system. He improved the telegraph, telephone, and motion-picture equipment. He waged the 'War of Currents' with Nikola Tesla, promoting direct current against alternating current. He founded General Electric. He held more than 1,000 US patents. He was a convinced practitioner, conducting thousands of experiments. He died in West Orange, New Jersey. Edison transformed invention into a system, creating the 'idea factory' model and proving that relentless hard work matters more than a flash of genius.

Бенджамин Франклин.name: Benjamin Franklin
Бенджамин Франклин.description: (1706–1790) American scientist, inventor, politician, diplomat, writer, and one of the Founding Fathers of the United States. Born in Boston to a soap-maker's family, the fifteenth of seventeen children. He worked in his brother's printing shop and at 17 ran away to Philadelphia. He became a publisher, founded the 'Pennsylvania Gazette' and 'Poor Richard's Almanack,' famous for aphorisms about work and thrift. He studied electricity, invented the lightning rod, created bifocal spectacles, and improved the stove. He founded the first public library, postal service, fire brigade, and Philadelphia Academy (later the University of Pennsylvania). He participated in drafting the Declaration of Independence and the US Constitution. He served as envoy to France during the War of Independence, securing the French alliance. He signed the Paris Peace of 1783. He died in Philadelphia. Franklin is a symbol of the American Enlightenment, self-made success, and the fusion of science, practice, and civic virtue.

Джеймс Ватт.name: James Watt
Джеймс Ватт.description: (1736–1819) Scottish engineer and inventor, a key figure of the Industrial Revolution. Born in Greenock to a shipwright and trader's family. He worked as a maker of mathematical instruments in Glasgow. In 1764, while repairing a model of Newcomen's steam engine, he identified its main flaw—heat loss from cooling the cylinder. He designed a separate condenser for steam, dramatically improving efficiency. In 1769 he obtained a patent on the improved steam engine. In 1775 he entered a partnership with industrialist Matthew Boulton, setting up production at the Soho Works in Birmingham. He created a double-acting engine that converted reciprocating motion into rotary motion. His steam engines became the heart of factories, mines, and foundries. The unit of power—the watt—is named in his honour. He was a Fellow of the Royal Society and a friend of Joseph Black and Adam Smith. He died at Heathfield. Watt transformed the steam engine into a universal industrial prime mover that changed the world.

Александр Грэм Белл.name: Alexander Graham Bell
Александр Грэм Белл.description: (1847–1922) Scottish-American scientist, inventor, and educator, creator of the telephone. Born in Edinburgh to a family of educators who developed the 'Visible Speech' method for the deaf. His mother was deaf, which shaped his interest in acoustics and speech. He moved to Canada, then to the US. He taught at a school for the deaf in Boston. He worked on transmitting speech by telegraph. On 10 March 1876 he transmitted the first intelligible words over the telephone: 'Mr Watson, come here—I want to see you.' He founded the Bell Telephone Company and grew wealthy from his patent. He continued research: aeronautics, the photophone, a metal detector. He co-founded the journal 'Science' and the National Geographic Society. He married his pupil Mabel Hubbard, deaf from childhood. He died in Nova Scotia. Bell transformed the voice into an electrical signal, changing the way humans communicate and remaining a symbol of connection between people.

Карл Бенц.name: Karl Benz
Карл Бенц.description: (1844–1929) German engineer and inventor, creator of the world's first series-produced motor vehicle with an internal-combustion engine, pioneer of the automobile industry. Born in Karlsruhe to a locomotive driver's family. He studied mechanical engineering at the Polytechnic University. He worked as a mechanic and designer. In 1871 he founded a mechanical workshop in Mannheim. In 1885 he created the Benz Patent-Motorwagen—a three-wheeled vehicle with a single-cylinder four-stroke engine. In 1886 he obtained a patent on a 'vehicle with a gas engine.' In 1888 his wife Bertha secretly drove 100 km, proving the practicality of the invention. He founded Benz & Cie and established series production. He competed with Daimler; their companies later merged into Mercedes-Benz. He greatly improved the carburettor, differential, and other key automobile components. He died in Ladenburg. Benz launched the era of personal mobility and became a symbol of technical courage and faith in the future.

Джеймс Джойс.name: James Joyce
Джеймс Джойс.description: (1882–1941) Irish modernist writer, one of the most influential prose writers of the 20th century. Born in Dublin to a civil servant's family. He studied at Jesuit colleges and at University College Dublin. In 1904 he left Ireland with Nora Barnacle, living in Trieste, Zurich, and Paris. He debuted with the story collection 'Dubliners' (1914). The novel 'A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man' (1916) is an autobiographical work about the development of an artist. 'Ulysses' (1922)—an epic of one day in Dublin, a parallel to Homer's 'Odyssey,' the pinnacle of the stream-of-consciousness technique—caused scandal and legal proceedings. 'Finnegans Wake' (1939) is an experimental novel on the border of dream and language, saturated with puns and neologisms. Joyce made Dublin a world literary capital, extending the boundaries of the novel and language. He died in Zurich. He remains a symbol of literary innovation and the inexhaustible complexity of the word.

Эрих Мария Ремарк.name: Erich Maria Remarque
Эрих Мария Ремарк.description: (1898–1970) German writer, one of the leading voices of the 'Lost Generation' and author of anti-war and humanist novels. Born in Osnabrück to a bookbinder's family. He fought in World War I and was wounded. He worked as a teacher, journalist, and advertising copywriter. His novel 'All Quiet on the Western Front' (1929)—a merciless portrayal of trench warfare from a soldier's perspective—became a world bestseller and was adapted for the screen. The Nazis burned the book as 'treasonous.' Remarque emigrated to Switzerland, then to the US. He wrote 'Three Comrades,' 'Arch of Triumph,' 'A Time to Love and a Time to Die,' and 'The Black Obelisk.' His novels tell of love, friendship, exile, and the attempt to remain human in an inhuman world. He was married to Paulette Goddard. He died in Locarno. Remarque remains the voice of a generation scarred by war and a symbol of humanism in the face of history's brutality.

Александр Сергеевич Пушкин.name: Alexander Pushkin
Александр Сергеевич Пушкин.description: (1799–1837) Russia's greatest poet, playwright, and prose writer, founder of the modern Russian literary language. Born in Moscow to an old noble family. He was raised by French tutors and from childhood immersed himself in Russian and French literature. He studied at the Tsarskoye Selo Lyceum, where he began writing poetry. Early fame was followed by southern exile and banishment to Mikhailovskoye. He wrote 'Ruslan and Lyudmila,' 'The Prisoner of the Caucasus,' 'The Fountain of Bakhchisaray,' and 'The Gypsies.' 'Boris Godunov' was the first genuine national tragedy. 'Eugene Onegin'—an 'encyclopaedia of Russian life' and the pinnacle of Russian poetry. 'The Little Tragedies,' 'The Bronze Horseman,' 'The Captain's Daughter,' fairy tales, and countless lyric masterpieces. He married Natalya Goncharova. He founded 'The Contemporary' journal. He was killed in a duel with d'Anthès in 1837. Pushkin created the Russian literary language, uniting folk speech with the bookish tradition. He remains the symbol of Russian culture and an unsurpassed master of words.

Джон Кеннеди.name: John F. Kennedy
Джон Кеннеди.description: (1917–1963) 35th President of the United States (1961–1963), the first Catholic and the youngest elected president in American history. Born in Brookline, Massachusetts, to a wealthy and influential family. He served in the Navy in World War II and became famous for rescuing the crew of a torpedo boat. He was elected to Congress and then to the Senate. In 1960 he defeated Nixon in the presidential election. The 'New Frontier' programme brought ambitious reforms in education, healthcare, and space exploration. He set the goal of landing a man on the Moon before the end of the decade. The Cuban Missile Crisis of 1962—a confrontation with the USSR—brought the world to the brink of nuclear war, which he helped avert. He supported the civil rights movement. On 22 November 1963 he was assassinated in Dallas; the official conclusion attributed the killing to Lee Harvey Oswald. Kennedy embodied optimism, youth, and faith in the possibilities of democracy. He remains a symbol of charismatic leadership and an unfinished era of hope.

Генрих II Валуа.name: Henry II of France
Генрих II Валуа.description: (1519–1559) King of France from the House of Valois, son of Francis I and Claude of France. Born in Saint-Germain-en-Laye, he spent years as a hostage in Spain following his father's defeat at Pavia. In 1533 he married Catherine de Medici. He ascended the throne after his father's death and continued the strengthening of absolute monarchy and centralisation of power. His mistress Diane de Poitiers exercised enormous influence at court. He ruthlessly persecuted the Huguenots, sharpening religious tensions. He waged wars against the Habsburgs, and French forces recaptured Calais from the English in 1558. On 30 June 1559, celebrating a peace treaty, he participated in a jousting tournament; Count Montgomery's lance pierced his visor and entered his eye. The king died ten days later. His death opened the era of the Wars of Religion; the throne passed to his sons Francis II, Charles IX, and Henry III. Henry II was the last king of France of the relatively stable Renaissance period before the bloody Wars of Faith.

Пётр I.name: Peter the Great
Пётр I.description: (1672–1725) First Emperor of All Russia, the Tsar-reformer who transformed Russia into a great European power. Born in Moscow, son of Tsar Alexis Mikhailovich. From 1682 he was co-ruler with his brother Ivan under Sophia's regency. From 1689 he ruled alone. He undertook the Grand Embassy to Europe (1697–1698), learning shipbuilding in Holland and England. He waged the Great Northern War against Sweden (1700–1721) and won at Poltava (1709). He founded St Petersburg (1703) and moved the capital there. He created a regular army and navy. He carried out sweeping reforms: the administrative system, Senate, colleges, the Table of Ranks; the Church was subordinated to the state; a new calendar and civil script were introduced. He promoted industry, education, and science. He founded the Academy of Sciences. He introduced assemblies and Western-style dress. He died in St Petersburg. Peter 'cut a window into Europe,' changing Russia's course; he remains a symbol of radical modernisation and the will for progress.

Екатерина II.name: Catherine the Great
Екатерина II.description: (1729–1796) Empress of All Russia (1762–1796), one of the most outstanding rulers in Russian history, the era of enlightened absolutism. Born in Stettin as Sophie Auguste Friederike of Anhalt-Zerbst, a German princess. In 1744 she came to Russia, converted to Orthodoxy, and married heir Peter Fyodorovich. In 1762 she led a palace coup, overthrew her husband (Peter III), and ascended the throne. She corresponded with Voltaire and Diderot and invited philosophers to court. She drafted the 'Nakaz' for the Legislative Commission, incorporating ideas of enlightened monarchy. She carried out a gubernatorial reform and educational reform. She expanded the empire: wars with Turkey, the annexation of Crimea, and the partitions of Poland. She founded the Hermitage, the Academy of Arts, and the Smolny Institute. Her reign was a golden age of culture and diplomatic success, but also the entrenchment of serfdom and the suppression of the Pugachev Revolt. She died at Tsarskoye Selo. Catherine transformed Russia into a great European power; she remains a symbol of enlightened absolutism and female rule.

Октавиан Август.name: Augustus
Октавиан Август.description: (63 BC–14 AD) First Roman Emperor (27 BC–14 AD), founder of the Principate, and adopted son and heir of Julius Caesar. Born as Gaius Octavius in Rome; after adoption he was named Gaius Julius Caesar Octavianus. After Caesar's assassination in 44 BC he entered the struggle for power. He formed the Second Triumvirate with Antony and Lepidus. He crushed the Republicans at Philippi. After the Triumvirate fell apart he defeated Mark Antony and Cleopatra at the naval Battle of Actium (31 BC). In 27 BC he 'restored the Republic,' receiving from the Senate the title Augustus and lifelong powers—creating the Principate, a monarchy beneath a republican façade. He ensured the Pax Romana—lasting peace and stability. He carried out administrative and military reforms. He transformed Rome into a marble capital. He patronised literature (Virgil, Horace, Ovid). He died at Nola. Augustus ended the civil wars and founded an empire that endured for centuries. He remains a symbol of political wisdom and the transformation of a republic into an empire.

Аристотель.name: Aristotle
Аристотель.description: (384–322 BC) Ancient Greek philosopher and scientist, one of antiquity's foremost thinkers and founder of the Peripatetic school. Born in Stagira to the family of a physician at the Macedonian court. At 17 he came to Athens and studied at Plato's Academy for about twenty years. After Plato's death he travelled, then was invited to Macedonia as tutor to the young Alexander. Returning to Athens, he founded the Lyceum, where he taught and conducted research. He created fundamental works on logic, metaphysics, ethics, politics, poetics, rhetoric, biology, and physics, and formulated the doctrine of categories and syllogisms. He developed virtue ethics and the principle of the 'golden mean,' and regarded the state as a natural form of communal life. After Alexander's death he left Athens due to anti-Macedonian sentiment and died in Chalcis. Aristotle's legacy shaped the development of European philosophy and science for many centuries.

Сенека.name: Seneca
Сенека.description: (c. 4 BC–65 AD) Roman Stoic philosopher, writer, and statesman. Born in Corduba (Spain) and raised in Rome, where he received a rhetorical and philosophical education. He served as senator, survived exile to Corsica, then returned to court as tutor to Emperor Nero. In the early years of Nero's reign he helped govern the state, then withdrew from public affairs. He wrote the treatises 'On the Shortness of Life,' 'On Anger,' 'On Mercy,' and 'On Tranquillity of Mind,' as well as 'Letters to Lucilius,' developing the practical ethics of Stoicism. In 65 AD he was accused of involvement in the Pisonian conspiracy and, on Nero's orders, was compelled to take his own life. Seneca became a symbol of Stoic composure and a moral philosophy addressed to everyday life.

Галилео Галилей.name: Galileo Galilei
Галилео Галилей.description: (1564–1642) Italian astronomer, physicist, and engineer, one of the key figures of the Scientific Revolution. Born in Pisa, he studied medicine but turned to mathematics and natural philosophy. He taught in Pisa and Padua. In 1609 he improved the spyglass and turned it on the sky: he discovered mountains on the Moon, the phases of Venus, Jupiter's moons, and the stellar nature of the Milky Way—powerful arguments against geocentrism. He studied the motion of bodies, inertia, and the pendulum, laying the foundations of classical mechanics. In 1632 he published 'Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems,' after which he was condemned by the Inquisition in 1633 and spent the rest of his life under house arrest. Despite the ban he continued working and wrote 'Two New Sciences.' Galileo became a symbol of the scientific method and the courage of reason before authority.

Франц Кафка.name: Franz Kafka
Франц Кафка.description: (1883–1924) Prague German-language writer of Jewish origin, one of the most influential authors of the 20th century. Born in Prague, he trained as a lawyer and worked in an insurance office. He wrote prose that blends the everyday with disturbing absurdity and the sense of impersonal power. He created the novella 'The Metamorphosis,' and the novels 'The Trial' and 'The Castle,' along with many stories and diaries. During his lifetime he published little, doubted the value of his own writing, and asked his friend Max Brod to destroy his manuscripts—but Brod preserved and published them posthumously. Kafka suffered from tuberculosis and died at 40. His name became an adjective: 'Kafkaesque' denotes a world in which a person confronts incomprehensible rules, bureaucracy, and existential dread.

Ада Лавлейс.name: Ada Lovelace
Ада Лавлейс.description: (1815–1852) English mathematician and writer, known for her work on Charles Babbage's analytical engine. Daughter of the poet Lord Byron and Anne Isabella Milbanke; she was educated with an emphasis on mathematics and logic. In 1843 she published a translation of Luigi Menabrea's paper on the analytical engine with extensive 'Notes' in which she described the machine's potential to work with symbols as well as numbers. Her notes contain an algorithm for computing Bernoulli numbers, often cited as one of the first programs ever written for a computing machine. Lovelace reflected on the future of computation, music, and science, stressing the role of imagination in discovery. She died at 36. Today Ada Lovelace is regarded as a symbol of the early history of programming and the union of mathematics with creative thinking.

Антон Чехов.name: Anton Chekhov
Антон Чехов.description: (1860–1904) Russian writer and playwright, one of the greatest masters of short prose and a reformer of theatre. Born in Taganrog, he studied medicine at Moscow University and called medicine his 'lawful spouse' all his life. He wrote stories in which he portrayed characters and everyday life with extraordinary precision, combining humour and pathos. He authored 'The Seagull,' 'Uncle Vanya,' 'Three Sisters,' and 'The Cherry Orchard,' all staged by the Moscow Art Theatre, transforming theatrical language. He made a journey to Sakhalin and wrote a documentary study of prison life and the lives of exiles. He suffered from tuberculosis and died at Badenweiler. Chekhov remains a symbol of humanism, precise observation, and the art of speaking about what matters most without grand gestures.

Лао-цзы.name: Laozi
Лао-цзы.description: (6th–5th c. BC) Ancient Chinese sage traditionally credited with authorship of the 'Tao Te Ching' ('The Classic of the Way and Its Power') and the founding of the Taoist philosophical tradition. The historicity of Laozi and the exact dates of his life remain subjects of scholarly debate; most researchers associate the text with the Warring States period (5th–3rd c. BC) and his figure with accumulated oral traditions. According to later legend, Laozi served as an archivist at the Zhou court, then, disillusioned with the realm, rode westward. At a border pass a guard asked him to leave behind his teaching—and so the brief treatise on the Tao and de came to be. The 'Tao Te Ching' teaches following naturalness, valuing simplicity, avoiding violence and extremes, and practising wu wei—action without forcing, in harmony with the flow of things. The text exerted an enormous influence on Chinese culture, philosophy, and religion. Laozi remains a symbol of quiet wisdom and the understanding that the true Way resists direct description.

Сунь-цзы.name: Sun Tzu
Сунь-цзы.description: (544–496 BC) Ancient Chinese strategist traditionally credited with the treatise 'The Art of War' ('Sunzi Bingfa')—one of the most influential works on strategy, military affairs, and management in world history. The historicity of Sun Tzu and the exact authorship of the treatise remain subjects of scholarly discussion; the text probably took shape during the Warring States period (5th–3rd c. BC), possibly on the basis of earlier oral traditions. According to Sima Qian's 'Records of the Grand Historian,' Sun Wu was a military commander of the state of Wu in the 6th century BC. 'The Art of War' systematises principles of victory: the importance of intelligence and information, flexibility and adaptation to circumstances, the role of morale and troop discipline, logistics and resource management, and a preference for winning without direct confrontation ('Supreme excellence consists in breaking the enemy's resistance without fighting'). The treatise exerted a profound influence on military thought in China, Japan, and the West, and its principles have come to be applied in politics, business, and negotiation. Sun Tzu remains a symbol of strategic thinking and the art of winning while preserving strength.

Авиценна.name: Avicenna
Авиценна.description: (980–1037) Persian polymath, physician, and philosopher, known in Europe as Avicenna, one of the key figures of the Islamic Golden Age. Born near Bukhara, he displayed an aptitude for the sciences and medicine from an early age, treated at royal courts, and held administrative posts. His principal medical work, the 'Canon of Medicine,' systematised the knowledge of ancient and Eastern medicine and remained a standard textbook across different parts of the world for centuries. His philosophical corpus includes the 'Book of Healing' and other treatises in which he developed the Aristotelian tradition, reasoning about the mind, causality, and being. Avicenna combined medical practice with an encyclopaedic drive to organise knowledge. He died in Hamadan. He remains a symbol of scientific systematisation, clinical thinking, and the union of medicine with philosophy.

Гипатия Александрийская.name: Hypatia of Alexandria
Гипатия Александрийская.description: (c. 355–415) Philosopher and mathematician of late antiquity, one of the most famous learned women of the ancient world. She lived and taught in Alexandria; daughter of the scholar Theon of Alexandria. Hypatia worked in mathematics, astronomy, and philosophy, headed a school in the Neoplatonic tradition, and taught pupils drawn from the city's elite. Her name is associated with commentaries on ancient mathematical and astronomical works (including Diophantus, Apollonius, and Ptolemy), though the exact scope of her surviving writings remains a matter of scholarly reconstruction. In the climate of political and religious conflict in Alexandria she was killed in 415 by a mob, and her death became a symbol of the tragic collision between science, power, and fanaticism. Hypatia remains a model of intellectual honesty, rationality, and a scholar's courage.

Микеланджело Буонарроти.name: Michelangelo
Микеланджело Буонарроти.description: (1475–1564) Italian Renaissance artist, one of the greatest masters in the history of art—sculptor, painter, architect, and poet. Born in Caprese near Arezzo, he grew up in Florence and studied in the circle of the Medici. He became famous as a sculptor: the 'Pietà' (Rome), 'David' (Florence), and 'Moses.' Commissioned by Pope Julius II, between 1508 and 1512 he painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel, creating a monumental cycle, and later executed 'The Last Judgement' on the altar wall. In his mature years he worked as an architect and became the principal architect of St Peter's Basilica in Rome, determining its appearance. Michelangelo united classical harmony with dramatic power of form and made the human body the supreme bearer of spiritual tension. He died in Rome, leaving a legacy that determined European art for centuries.

Иоганн Себастьян Бах.name: Johann Sebastian Bach
Иоганн Себастьян Бах.description: (1685–1750) German composer and organist of the Baroque era, one of the greatest musicians in history. Born in Eisenach into a musical family; orphaned early and trained as an organist and composer. He worked in Arnstadt, Mühlhausen, and Weimar, then served as Kapellmeister in Köthen, and from 1723 as Cantor of the Thomaskirche in Leipzig. He created a vast body of music: cantatas, chorales, organ works, 'The Well-Tempered Clavier,' the 'Brandenburg Concertos,' 'St Matthew Passion,' and the 'Mass in B minor.' His art raised polyphony and counterpoint to their highest perfection, combining mathematical rigour with spiritual depth. During his lifetime he was better known as an organist; in the 19th century he was rediscovered and recognised as a genius. He died in Leipzig. Bach remains a symbol of harmony, discipline, and the power of musical thought.

Нельсон Мандела.name: Nelson Mandela
Нельсон Мандела.description: (1918–2013) South African political leader and anti-apartheid activist, the first Black president of South Africa (1994–1999). Born in Mvezo, a member of the Xhosa people, he received a legal education. He joined the African National Congress (ANC) and fought against racial segregation. After the regime intensified repression he supported the creation of an armed wing of the ANC, was arrested, and convicted at the Rivonia Trial (1964) to life imprisonment. He spent 27 years in jail, mainly on Robben Island. Released in 1990, he led negotiations on dismantling apartheid and the transition to democracy. In 1993, together with F. W. de Klerk, he received the Nobel Peace Prize. As president he championed national reconciliation and created the Truth and Reconciliation Commission. Mandela became a symbol of resilience, dignity, and the struggle for equal rights.

Мария Терезия.name: Maria Theresa
Мария Терезия.description: (1717–1780) Ruler of the Habsburg Monarchy (1740–1780), Archduchess of Austria, Queen of Hungary and Bohemia, one of the most influential female rulers of 18th-century Europe.
