Born in Vienna in 1717, daughter of Emperor Charles VI. After his death she inherited the Habsburg territories, which led to the War of the Austrian Succession; she lost Silesia but preserved her core territories and consolidated her power. She was the wife of Francis Stephen of Lorraine (Emperor Francis I) and mother of 16 children, including future Emperor Joseph II and Marie Antoinette. She carried out sweeping reforms: centralisation of administration, reorganisation of the army and finances, development of school education, and streamlining of the administrative system. Although her policies combined elements of enlightened governance with traditional views, Maria Theresa significantly modernised the state and strengthened the Habsburg position in Europe. She died in 1780.

Сунь Ятсен.name: Sun Yat-sen
Сунь Ятсен.description: (1866–1925) Chinese revolutionary, political thinker, and one of the founders of the Republic of China. Born in Guangdong Province, he received a medical education and practised as a physician. In the late 19th century he joined the anti-Qing revolutionary movement, organised alliances and uprisings, and was often in exile. After the Xinhai Revolution of 1911, which brought down the Qing dynasty, he became provisional president of the Republic of China in 1912. He founded the Kuomintang (Chinese Nationalist Party) and developed the programme of the 'Three Principles of the People.' In his final years he sought to unify the country and build a modern state, cooperating with various forces in pursuit of national unity. He died in 1925. Sun Yat-sen remains a symbol of the republican idea and the modernisation of China.

Изабелла Кастильская.name: Isabella I of Castile
Изабелла Кастильская.description: (1451–1504) Queen of Castile (1474–1504), one of the key figures of late medieval Spain. Born in 1451 into the House of Trastámara. In 1469 she married Ferdinand of Aragon, laying the foundation for the unification of the Spanish crowns. Under Isabella and Ferdinand the Reconquista was completed: in 1492 Granada—the last Muslim emirate on the Iberian Peninsula—was taken. That same year the Crown supported Christopher Columbus's expedition, which opened the way for Europeans to the Americas. Isabella's era is also associated with a strengthening of royal authority and religious policy: the creation of the Spanish Inquisition and the Alhambra Decree (1492) expelling the Jews—measures with grave consequences. She died in 1504. Isabella remains a symbol of the formation of unified Spain and the beginning of Spanish global expansion.

Мария Монтессори.name: Maria Montessori
Мария Монтессори.description: (1870–1952) Italian physician and educator, creator of the Montessori educational system. Born in Chiaravalle, she studied medicine and became one of Italy's first female doctors. She worked with children with developmental disabilities, then developed an approach to learning based on observation, independent activity, and a specially prepared environment. In 1907 she opened the 'Casa dei Bambini' (Children's House) in Rome, where she applied her methods with children from poor families. Her system spread across the world and exerted an enormous influence on pre-school and primary education. Montessori wrote books and gave lectures, advocating humane child-rearing and the development of independence. During Mussolini's dictatorship and the Second World War she lived and worked outside Italy, including in India. She died in the Netherlands in 1952. Montessori remains a symbol of respectful, scientifically grounded education.

Оскар Уайльд.name: Oscar Wilde
Оскар Уайльд.description: (1854–1900) Irish writer, playwright, and poet, one of the most celebrated wits of English literature. Born in Dublin, he studied at Trinity College and Oxford. He became a prominent figure in London cultural life, championing Aestheticism. He wrote the novel 'The Picture of Dorian Gray,' collections of fairy tales and essays, and plays including 'The Importance of Being Earnest.' In 1895 he was convicted of 'gross indecency' under the laws of the time and served two years in prison; the experience of imprisonment was reflected in 'The Ballad of Reading Gaol' and the letter 'De Profundis.' After his release he lived in France in poverty and died in Paris. Wilde remains a symbol of artistic freedom, brilliant language, and the tragedy of a person colliding with Victorian morality.

Данте Алигьери.name: Dante Alighieri
Данте Алигьери.description: (1265–1321) Italian poet and thinker, author of 'The Divine Comedy'—one of the greatest works of world literature. Born in Florence, he participated in the city's political life and was driven into exile after a change of power. He spent most of his life outside Florence, creating his major works there. 'The Divine Comedy' describes a symbolic journey through Hell, Purgatory, and Paradise and became the summit of medieval poetics, philosophy, and theology, written in the vernacular Italian tongue. Dante also wrote the treatises 'De vulgari eloquentia' and 'De Monarchia,' reflecting on political order and language. He died in Ravenna. Dante became a symbol of Italian culture and an example of how poetry can serve as a map of the world and the conscience.

Иоганн Вольфганг фон Гёте.name: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
Иоганн Вольфганг фон Гёте.description: (1749–1832) German writer, poet, and thinker, one of the central figures of European culture. Born in Frankfurt am Main and trained as a lawyer. He won early fame with the novel 'The Sorrows of Young Werther,' which became an emblem of the 'Storm and Stress' era. He spent most of his life in Weimar, where he served at court and engaged in government affairs as well as science and art. His principal work is the dramatic poem 'Faust,' on which he laboured for decades. Goethe wrote lyric poetry, prose, drama, and carried out natural-philosophical research (including studies of colour). He shaped the image of the classical humanist who seeks a harmony of reason, feeling, and action. He died in Weimar. Goethe remains a symbol of the European classical spirit and the idea of personal development.

Пётр Ильич Чайковский.name: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky
Пётр Ильич Чайковский.description: (1840–1893) Russian composer, one of the most celebrated Romantic-era composers. Born in Votkinsk, he received a legal education but devoted his life to music, studying at the St Petersburg Conservatory. He composed six symphonies, concertos, operas, and ballets, among them 'Swan Lake,' 'Sleeping Beauty,' and 'The Nutcracker.' His music combines vivid melodic invention, drama, and mastery of orchestration. Tchaikovsky worked intensely, experienced inner crises, yet left an enormous artistic world beloved by audiences worldwide. He died in 1893; the official cause of death was cholera. Tchaikovsky remains a symbol of the Russian musical soul and the Romantic power of melody.

Фредди Меркьюри.name: Freddie Mercury
Фредди Меркьюри.description: (1946–1991) British singer and songwriter, frontman of Queen, one of the most distinctive voices in rock history. Born in Zanzibar as Farrokh Bulsara, he later moved to Great Britain. In 1970 he formed Queen with Brian May and Roger Taylor, becoming its lead vocalist and one of the principal songwriters. He performed songs that became classics: 'Bohemian Rhapsody,' 'We Are the Champions,' 'Somebody to Love,' and many others. He was renowned for his powerful vocal range, charisma, and unique stage presence; Queen's performance at Live Aid (1985) is regarded as one of the greatest in history. He died in 1991 from complications related to AIDS. Mercury remains a symbol of freedom of self-expression and the power of live performance.

Марлон Брандо.name: Marlon Brando
Марлон Брандо.description: (1924–2004) American actor, one of the key figures of 20th-century cinema, associated with the development of psychological acting and the Method. Born in Omaha, he trained as an actor and performed on stage. He became famous for the role of Stanley Kowalski in 'A Streetcar Named Desire' and became an icon of post-war cinema. He played Vito Corleone in 'The Godfather' and received an Academy Award, which in 1973 he publicly refused to accept, protesting the treatment of Native Americans. He is also known for his roles in 'On the Waterfront,' 'Apocalypse Now,' and other films. Brando exerted a profound influence on the art of acting, making naturalness and inner truth a new standard. He died in Los Angeles.

Моисей.name: Moses
Моисей.description: (13th c. BC) Prophet and lawgiver in the Jewish, Christian, and Islamic traditions, the central figure of the Exodus narrative. According to religious tradition, Moses led the Israelites out of Egypt and received the Law (the Torah) on Mount Sinai, concluding a covenant between God and the people. His image is associated with the idea of liberation from slavery, responsibility before the law, and a spiritual journey through trials. The historical reconstruction of Moses's life and the details of the Exodus remains a subject of scholarly debate, as the sources are religious-traditional in character. Nevertheless, Moses is one of the most influential figures in the history of religion—a symbol of moral law, leadership, and fidelity to the path.

Святой Франциск Ассизский.name: Saint Francis of Assisi
Святой Франциск Ассизский.description: (1181/1182–1226) Italian Catholic saint, founder of the Franciscan order, one of the most venerated Christian ascetics. Born in Assisi to a wealthy merchant family, in his youth he led a worldly life but underwent a spiritual transformation and chose the path of poverty and service. He preached simplicity, peace, care for the poor, and love for all creation. He founded a brotherhood that became the Order of the Friars Minor (Franciscans); his spirituality influenced the entire Western Christian tradition. He is credited with the 'Canticle of the Sun' and a special relationship with nature; later sources mention the stigmata. He was canonised in 1228. Francis of Assisi remains a symbol of humility, mercy, and peacemaking.

Авраам Линкольн.name: Abraham Lincoln
Авраам Линкольн.description: (1809–1865) American statesman, 16th President of the United States, who led the country during the Civil War. Born into a poor family in Kentucky, he educated himself and worked as a lawyer. He gained political prominence as an opponent of the expansion of slavery. Elected president in 1860, he saw several southern states secede after his victory, triggering the war (1861–1865). In 1863 he issued the Emancipation Proclamation, declaring the freedom of enslaved people in rebel territories, and later supported the Thirteenth Amendment abolishing slavery throughout the United States. He delivered the Gettysburg Address—one of the most celebrated political speeches in history. In April 1865 he was fatally wounded in an assassination at Ford's Theatre. Lincoln remains a symbol of national unity, civic leadership, and the fight for freedom.

Королева Виктория.name: Queen Victoria
Королева Виктория.description: (1819–1901) Queen of the United Kingdom (1837–1901) and Empress of India (from 1876), one of the most prominent figures of British monarchy. Born in 1819, she ascended the throne at 18. Her reign gave its name to the 'Victorian era'—a period of industrial growth, social and cultural transformation, and expansion of the British Empire. In 1840 she married Prince Albert; their family life and numerous children made Victoria the centre of European dynastic connections. After Albert's death in 1861 she spent years in mourning. In the latter half of her reign she became a symbol of stability and tradition. She died in 1901. Victoria remains a symbol of the imperial 19th century, monarchical duty, and the social morality of her time.

Стивен Хокинг.name: Stephen Hawking
Стивен Хокинг.description: (1942–2018) British theoretical physicist and science communicator, one of the most celebrated scientists of modern times. He worked in cosmology and the theory of black holes and proposed the theoretical effect of black hole radiation known as 'Hawking radiation.' For many years he held the Lucasian Professorship at Cambridge University. In his youth he was diagnosed with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis; despite the severe disease he continued his scientific work and became a symbol of intellectual resilience. He authored 'A Brief History of Time,' making cosmology accessible to a wide audience. Hawking made a major contribution to science and its popularisation and remains a symbol of curiosity and the power of the mind.

Алан Тьюринг.name: Alan Turing
Алан Тьюринг.description: (1912–1954) British mathematician and cryptanalyst, one of the founders of theoretical computer science and artificial intelligence. In 1936 he described an abstract computational model known as the 'Turing machine' and contributed to the understanding of computability. During the Second World War he worked at Bletchley Park, participating in the decryption of German communications; his contribution is associated with the cryptanalysis of the Enigma system. After the war he worked on computing and questions of machine intelligence, proposing the 'Turing test' as a criterion for simulating human dialogue. In post-war Britain he was persecuted for his homosexuality—a tragic chapter in his biography. He died in 1954. Today Turing is a symbol of scientific genius and a warning about the cost of discrimination.

Чарльз Диккенс.name: Charles Dickens
Чарльз Диккенс.description: (1812–1870) English writer, one of the most popular novelists of the Victorian era. Born in Portsmouth, he experienced poverty in his youth: because of his father's debts he worked in a factory, leaving a deep mark on his life. He began his career as a journalist, then achieved fame through novels published in instalments. He wrote 'Oliver Twist,' 'David Copperfield,' 'Bleak House,' 'Great Expectations,' and 'A Christmas Carol.' His works combine social satire with sympathy for the downtrodden, vivid characters, and dramatic plots. Dickens influenced public opinion and the discussion of reform. He died in 1870. He remains a symbol of Victorian literature and artistic compassion for the human being.

Джейн Остин.name: Jane Austen
Джейн Остин.description: (1775–1817) English writer, one of the key figures of world prose, a master of the social novel and ironic psychological observation. Born in Steventon to a clergyman's family, she lived in provincial England. Her novels depict the life of the gentry and middle classes, focusing on manners, upbringing, and social expectations, especially regarding women. She wrote 'Pride and Prejudice,' 'Sense and Sensibility,' 'Emma,' 'Mansfield Park,' and 'Persuasion.' During her lifetime she published anonymously and received recognition, but her worldwide fame came later. She died in 1817. Austen remains a symbol of precise irony and deep understanding of human character.

Эрнест Хемингуэй.name: Ernest Hemingway
Эрнест Хемингуэй.description: (1899–1961) American writer and journalist, one of the most influential prose writers of the 20th century, Nobel Prize laureate in Literature (1954). He worked as a reporter, served as a war correspondent, and participated in events of the First World War, covering conflicts in Europe. He wrote novels and novellas including 'A Farewell to Arms,' 'For Whom the Bell Tolls,' 'The Sun Also Rises,' and 'The Old Man and the Sea.' His style is noted for its terseness and the 'iceberg principle,' in which the most important things lie beneath the surface. Hemingway lived between Europe, Cuba, and the United States, surviving trauma and illness. He died in 1961. He remains a symbol of supremely honest prose and the image of stoic endurance in the face of life.

Дж. Р. Р. Толкин.name: J.R.R. Tolkien
Дж. Р. Р. Толкин.description: (1892–1973) English writer, philologist, and professor, author of 'The Hobbit' and 'The Lord of the Rings.' Born in South Africa, he grew up in England. He fought in World War I and then devoted his life to academic work, studying Old English language and literature. He created the legendarium of Middle-earth—'The Silmarillion,' 'The Hobbit,' 'The Lord of the Rings'—in which mythology is bound to the invented languages he developed. His works explore friendship, the evil of the lust for power, the cost of war, and the significance of small acts of courage. Tolkien became one of the founders of modern fantasy literature and exerted an enormous influence on 20th-century culture. He died in 1973. He remains a symbol of mythmaking and the power of language.

Элвис Пресли.name: Elvis Presley
Элвис Пресли.description: (1935–1977) American singer and actor, one of the most famous figures in popular music of the 20th century, often called the 'King of Rock and Roll.' Born in Tupelo, Mississippi, he grew up in Memphis. In the 1950s he became a star by blending rhythm and blues, country, and rock and roll; his performances transformed stage culture. He recorded many hits and appeared in a number of films. In 1968 he returned to the stage with a television 'comeback' special, and in the 1970s gave celebrated concerts including appearances in Las Vegas. His life was marked by an intense schedule and health problems. He died in 1977 at Graceland. Elvis remains a symbol of the birth of mass pop culture and the energy of rock and roll.

Майкл Джексон.name: Michael Jackson
Майкл Джексон.description: (1958–2009) American singer, dancer, and entertainer, one of the most famous figures in pop music. He began his career in childhood with The Jackson 5, then became a solo star. The album 'Thriller' (1982) is one of the best-selling of all time, and his music videos and stage routines (including the moonwalk) became cultural symbols. Jackson was known for his drive for perfection in recording and staging shows, as well as for his charitable work. His life was accompanied by enormous public attention and controversial press coverage. He died in 2009. Michael Jackson remains a symbol of global pop culture and performance innovation.

Чарли Чаплин.name: Charlie Chaplin
Чарли Чаплин.description: (1889–1977) English actor, director, and composer, one of the central figures of silent cinema and world cinematography. Born in London into a poor family, he began performing early. He created the character of the Tramp, which became a symbol of humanity and irony. He directed and starred in 'The Kid,' 'The Gold Rush,' 'City Lights,' and 'Modern Times.' In 1940 he released 'The Great Dictator'—a satire on totalitarianism. In the 1950s he came under political pressure in the US and lived in Switzerland. He died in 1977. Chaplin remains a symbol of art that defends human dignity through laughter.

Мэрилин Монро.name: Marilyn Monroe
Мэрилин Монро.description: (1926–1962) American actress and model, one of the most recognisable icons of 20th-century popular culture. Born as Norma Jeane Mortenson (Baker), she endured a difficult childhood and early life. She became a Hollywood star in the 1950s, appearing in 'Gentlemen Prefer Blondes,' 'Some Like It Hot,' and other films. She was known for a combination of comedic talent and screen charisma. She studied acting and aspired to more serious roles. Her life was accompanied by intense press attention, complicated relationships, and health problems. She died in 1962; her death was officially ruled a probable suicide, though the circumstances have been disputed. Monroe remains a symbol of Hollywood glamour and human vulnerability.

Фрида Кало.name: Frida Kahlo
Фрида Кало.description: (1907–1954) Mexican painter, known above all for self-portraits and works in which personal pain is fused with national symbolism. Born in Coyoacán (Mexico City), she suffered a severe accident in her youth whose consequences accompanied her throughout her life and were reflected in her art. She was embedded in the cultural and political life of Mexico and was married to the muralist Diego Rivera. Her paintings unite realism, symbolism, and elements akin to Surrealism, although Kahlo herself insisted she painted her reality. She died in 1954. Frida Kahlo became a symbol of artistic honesty, female strength, and the right to speak of pain and identity in one's own voice.

Жюль Верн.name: Jules Verne
Жюль Верн.description: (1828–1905) French writer, one of the founders of science fiction and one of the most translated authors in the world. Born in Nantes, he studied law in Paris but devoted himself to literature. In 1863 he published his first novel in the 'Extraordinary Voyages' series—'Five Weeks in a Balloon.' He wrote 'Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas' (Captain Nemo and the submarine Nautilus), 'Around the World in Eighty Days,' 'The Mysterious Island,' 'Journey to the Centre of the Earth,' 'From the Earth to the Moon,' and dozens of other novels. He anticipated many inventions: submarines, space flight, and helicopters. His books combine adventure, scientific romanticism, and faith in progress. He died in Amiens. Jules Verne remains a symbol of the dream of exploring the world and the cosmos.

Рене Декарт.name: René Descartes
Рене Декарт.description: (1596–1650) French philosopher and mathematician, one of the key figures of early modern philosophy and the Scientific Revolution. Born in La Haye (Touraine), he studied at a Jesuit college and served in the army. He developed analytic geometry, uniting algebra and geometry (Cartesian coordinates). In 'Discourse on the Method' (1637) he formulated principles of scientific knowledge. The famous 'Cogito, ergo sum' ('I think, therefore I am') became the foundation of his philosophy: from radical doubt to the certainty of thought and the existence of God. He distinguished res cogitans (soul, thought) from res extensa (body, extension). His rationalism and method of doubt influenced philosophy and science. He died in Stockholm at the court of Queen Christina. Descartes remains a symbol of clarity of thought and philosophical rationalism.

Марко Поло.name: Marco Polo
Марко Поло.description: (1254–1324) Venetian merchant and traveller, author of 'The Travels of Marco Polo' ('The Description of the World'), one of the most important sources on 13th-century Asia. Born in Venice to a merchant family. In 1271 he set out with his father and uncle to Asia, reaching the court of the Mongol khan Kublai in China. He served at the khan's court for about 17 years and carried out diplomatic missions. He returned to Venice in 1295. In 1298 he was captured by the Genoese and in prison dictated his memoirs to Rustichello of Pisa. The book described the court of Kublai Khan, paper money, coal, the Grand Canal, and much else. For a long time his accounts were met with scepticism, but many details have since been confirmed. He influenced European conceptions of the East and inspired travellers, including Columbus. Marco Polo remains a symbol of the spirit of discovery and a bridge between civilisations.

Елизавета I.name: Elizabeth I
Елизавета I.description: (1533–1603) Queen of England and Ireland (1558–1603), the last of the Tudor dynasty, the 'Virgin Queen.' Born in 1533, daughter of Henry VIII and Anne Boleyn. She survived disgrace under her sister Mary Tudor's reign. She ascended the throne at 25 after Mary's death. She restored Anglicanism but pursued a moderate religious policy. She refused to marry, using the prospect of marriage as a diplomatic instrument. She supported maritime expeditions (Drake, Raleigh) and the struggle against Spain. The defeat of the Spanish Armada in 1588 secured England's position. She patronised the arts: Shakespeare and Marlowe flourished at her court. Her era—the 'Elizabethan age'—is regarded as the golden age of English culture. She died in 1603. Elizabeth I remains a symbol of powerful female rule and England's flourishing.

Платон.name: Plato
Платон.description: (428–348 BC) Ancient Greek philosopher, pupil of Socrates, teacher of Aristotle, and founder of the philosophical school—the Academy in Athens. Born into an aristocratic family in Athens. He received a fine education in music, gymnastics, and mathematics. At 20 he became Socrates' pupil, under whose influence he turned to philosophy. After Socrates' death (399 BC) he left Athens, travelled to Egypt, Italy, and Sicily. He returned to Athens in 387 BC and founded the Academy—the world's first philosophical school. He wrote in the form of dialogues, with Socrates often the main interlocutor. He created the doctrine of Ideas (Forms)—eternal, unchanging archetypes of which the things of the sensory world are copies. He developed an epistemology according to which the soul, before birth, dwelt in the world of Ideas and cognition is recollection of them. He created political philosophy: in 'The Republic' he described an ideal just state governed by philosopher-kings. His teaching influenced the entire development of Western philosophy. He died in Athens. Plato remains one of the greatest philosophers in history and the founder of idealism.

Фридрих Ницше.name: Friedrich Nietzsche
Фридрих Ницше.description: (1844–1900) German philosopher, poet, philologist, and composer, one of the most influential and controversial thinkers of the 19th century. Born in Röcken, Prussia, to a pastor's family. Orphaned early, he was raised by his mother and grandmother. He displayed exceptional ability and received the finest education. At 24 he became Professor of Classical Philology at the University of Basel. He soon left academia due to illness and disagreements with the scholarly community. He lived a wandering life in Italy, Switzerland, and France, in poverty and solitude. He created an original philosophy: proclaimed the 'death of God,' criticised Christian morality as 'slave morality,' and developed the concepts of the 'will to power,' the 'Übermensch,' and 'eternal recurrence.' He wrote in an aphoristic, poetic style: 'Thus Spoke Zarathustra,' 'Beyond Good and Evil,' 'On the Genealogy of Morality.' He suffered from mental illness and spent his last 11 years in a state of dementia. He died in Weimar. Nietzsche exerted an enormous influence on 20th-century philosophy, psychoanalysis, existentialism, and postmodernism. He remains a symbol of radical critique and creative freedom.

Виктор Цой.name: Viktor Tsoi
Виктор Цой.description: (1962–1990) Soviet rock musician, poet, and actor, leader of the group Kino. Born in Leningrad to an engineer father and a physical education teacher mother. He founded Kino in 1984 and became one of the defining voices of the rock movement of the perestroika era. He wrote songs that resonated with millions: 'Gruppa Krovi' ('Blood Type'), 'Kukushka' ('Cuckoo'), 'Zvezda po imeni Solntse' ('A Star Called the Sun'), 'Pachka Sigaret' ('A Pack of Cigarettes'), 'Spokoinaya Noch' ('Good Night')—lyrics that spoke of the path, the choice, and the refusal to compromise. He appeared in the cult film 'Igla' ('The Needle') directed by Rashid Nugmanov. He died in a road accident in Latvia in 1990. Viktor Tsoi remains a symbol of a whole generation, of sincerity, and of the unwillingness to make peace with oneself.
